ab_130.fact: AB 130 (Chapter 22, Statutes of 2025), effective 2025-06-30, sets a moratorium on new state and local building standards affecting residential units from 2025-10-01 to 2031-06-01, with listed exceptions (emergency health and safety standards, home hardening, and others). It amended Health and Safety Code 17958, 17958.5, 17958.7 and 18941.5.

supplements.note: Emergency standards last 180 days with two possible 90-day extensions unless made permanent (stated on the supplement record). Permanent status as of 2026-11-20: unconfirmed. parts.name: California Wildland-Urban Interface Code
parts.based_on_confirmed: read in source: History Note Appendix on the emergency supplement pages
parts.confirmation: Confirmed. Part 7 of the 2025 edition is the California Wildland-Urban Interface Code (BSC codes page; HCD IB 2025-03; history note). It adopts IWUIC 2024 with amendments relocated from the CBC (former Chapter 7A), CRC (former R337) and CFC. CRC R337 is now only a user note pointing to Part 7, and CRC R102.7 applies Part 7 in WUI areas.

numbering.finding: The 2025 CRC kept the IRC 2024 chapter 3 numbering (R309 sprinklers, R310 smoke alarms, R311 CO alarms, R312 room areas, R313 ceiling height, R318 egress, R319 escape openings, R320 handrails, R321 guards, R325 light/ventilation). California-only sections sit at R300, R328 (aging-in-place; was R327 in the 2022 CRC), R334 to R340.

crc_checks.note: Bathrooms, toilet rooms, laundry rooms: 6 ft 8 in (2032 mm). Sloped ceilings: 5 ft minimum and at least 50 percent of required area at 7 ft. Basement obstructions: 6 ft 4 in (1931 mm).

crc_checks.label: Natural light: glazed area as share of room floor area, minimum
crc_checks.amendment_basis: Number not in italics in the secondary copy; R325.1.1 is listed as an HCD amendment in the official matrix because of an added exception only.
crc_checks.note: The 8 percent figure is unamended. California added one exception (glazing may open into a passive solar energy collector), so the clause is listed as amended in the official matrix. Artificial-light exception: 6 footcandles (65 lux) at 30 in above floor.

crc_checks.label: Natural ventilation: openable area as share of room floor area, minimum
crc_checks.amendment_basis: Number not in italics; clause listed as amended in the official matrix because of exception wording.
crc_checks.note: The 4 percent figure is unamended. California changed the mechanical-ventilation exceptions to refer to the California Mechanical Code (0.35 air changes per hour whole-house system) and added a passive solar collector exception.

crc_checks.label: Bathroom window glazing, minimum (half openable), unless artificial light plus exhaust
crc_checks.amendment_basis: Exhaust rates are in California italics; R325.2 and R325.2.1 are listed as HCD amendments in the official matrix.
crc_checks.note: 3 sq ft is the IRC figure. California wrote the exhaust rates into the exception: 50 cfm (25 L/s) intermittent or 20 cfm (10 L/s) continuous, per California Mechanical Code Chapter 4. California-only R325.2.1: every bathroom with a tub or shower must have a mechanical exhaust fan (window alone does not count).

crc_checks.label: Smoke alarm locations
crc_checks.value: each sleeping room; outside each sleeping area near the bedrooms; each additional story incl. basements and habitable attics; not less than 3 ft from a bathroom door with tub/shower; hallway plus adjoining room where that room's ceiling is 24 in or more higher; room a sleeping loft opens to
crc_checks.amendment_basis: List items are not in italics; the pointer to R310.3.3 and all of R310.3.3, R310.4, R310.6 are California text in the secondary copy. Section R310 is an SFM adoption in the official matrix (SFM amendments are not itemised there).
crc_checks.note: The location list matches IRC 2024. California (State Fire Marshal) adds R310.3.3, an NFPA 72 extract: 20 ft from fixed cooking appliances (10 ft for photoelectric or ionization with silence switch, 6 ft photoelectric in tight plans), 36 in from forced-air supply registers and ceiling fan blade tips, not in spaces below 40 F or above 100 F. Interconnection (R310.4) and power source (R310.6) are California text. Alarms must be State Fire Marshal listed.

california_only.label: Automatic fire sprinklers required in new one- and two-family dwellings and townhouses
california_only.note: Not required for additions or alterations to buildings without sprinklers. ADU exception: detached ADU not over 1,200 sq ft (111.5 m2) on the same lot where the primary home has no sprinklers (Government Code 66313 definition). Design per R309 or NFPA 13D. IRC 2024 has the same R309 requirement; the ADU exception is California text. In the 2022 CRC this was R313.

california_only.label: Detached ADU floor area at or below which the sprinkler exception can apply
Guard height minimum (IRC: 36 in)
california_only.note: See crc_checks. Amendment status read on the official matrix.

california_only.label: Grab bar wall reinforcement band, at least one bathroom on the entry level: between these heights above finished floor
california_only.note: Reinforcement at least 2x8 nominal (1 1/2 in by 7 1/4 in actual). Tub: back-wall reinforcement for a lower bar with bottom edge not more than 6 in (152.4 mm) above the rim. Not needed in floors on concrete slab. R328 is California-only (HCD), listed in the official matrix; was R327 in the 2022 CRC.

california_only.note: Read on HCD's official summary form SHL 625 (Rev. 11/25), not on a page of the code. Raceway not required if a 40 A 208/240 V dedicated EV circuit is installed. Panel directory and raceway end marked 'EV CAPABLE' (4.106.4.1.1). ADUs and JADUs without added parking are exempt (4.106.4 exception 2).

california_only.note: Read on HCD's official summary form SHL 625 (Rev. 11/25), not on a page of the code. Charger circuits 40 A minimum with chargers not less than 30 A; load management must deliver at least 3.3 kW per station. Hotels and motels: 40 percent receptacles and 25 percent chargers (4.106.4.2.6).

california_only.note: One in every 25 such spaces (at least one) also needs an 8 ft (2438 mm) aisle, or 5 ft (1524 mm) aisle if the space is 12 ft (3658 mm) wide; slope not over 1:48 (2.083 percent).

california_only.note: Hotels and motels long-term: 1 per 25,000 sq ft, at least 2 (4.106.4.4.3).

california_only.note: Read on HCD's official summary form SHL 625 (Rev. 11/25), not on a page of the code.

california_only.note: Read on HCD's official summary form SHL 625 (Rev. 11/25), not on a page of the code.

Occupant recycling area required where this many multifamily units or more are built on a site
Sites disturbing less than this area must still manage construction storm water

california_only.code: California Wildland-Urban Interface Code 2025 (Part 7) / California Residential Code 2025 (Part 2.5)
california_only.clause: CRC R102.7, R337 user note; CWUIC 501.1, 503.1
california_only.note: Exempt: Group U accessory structures not over 120 sq ft (11 m2) at least 50 ft (15 240 mm) from applicable buildings; Group U agricultural buildings at least 50 ft away (CWUIC 501.1, read on emergency supplement pages). california_only.label: Accessory buildings near an applicable building: under 3 ft any size; over 120 sq ft between 3 ft and 50 ft: noncombustible or ignition-resistant construction
california_only.note: Read on the Final Express Terms only.

copyright.scope: Facts and citations only. Not advice.

copyright_holders.fact: The printed copyright notices of the 2025 parts could not be read: the ICC viewer blocked automated access and the errata PDFs carry no copyright page.

The official California amendments file for Part 3 describes the NEC as 'authored and published by the National Fire Protection Association' and marks the title line with a copyright sign after 'National Electrical Code'.

Older BSC publication agreements posted by Public.Resource.Org are reported to name the Commission as sole copyright owner of the California-only parts (for example the 2008 Part 11, and Parts 1, 6, 7, 8, 12) and to license ICC to publish the model-code-based parts. From a search summary; the agreements were not opened, and they predate the 2025 edition.
Model codes (IBC, IRC, IFC, IEBC, IWUIC by ICC; UMC, UPC by IAPMO; NEC by NFPA) are published under their developers' copyright claims; ICC runs a copyright permission request process.

free_viewer_terms.fact: Free access is read-only; the page shell states printing needs a Digital Codes Premium subscription. The U.S. Copyright Office case summary describes ICC as giving 'free, read-only access'. Full terms of use not read (captcha).
Requires creating a user login (stated on the BSC codes page). Terms not read.
Page-image flipbook viewer reachable without login. Terms not read.
BSC states Title 24 is viewable at no cost through several State Document Depository Libraries.

california_statutes.fact: (a) Commission publishes the code in full every three years, with supplements in between and separate emergency supplements. (d) The Commission may itself print and sell the code and incorporated materials only if they are not readily or reasonably available to the public; each state department concerned and each city and county must keep a current copy available for public inspection. (e) Each city and county must hold at least one current copy of Titles 8, 19, 20, 24 and 25 standards in the building official's office.

case_law.cite: International Code Council, Inc. v. UpCodes, Inc., No. 17 Civ. 6261 (VM), 2020 U.S. Dist. LEXIS 92324 (S.D.N.Y. May 27, 2020)
case_law.fact: On cross-motions for summary judgment the court concluded model codes as adopted into law are likely in the public domain and that posting them verbatim was fair use; fact disputes remained on redline versions showing unadopted model text offered to paying users.
case_law.later_history: A Second Circuit docket No. 21-826 exists; outcome and the current status of the S.D.N.Y. case: unconfirmed.

case_law.cite: American Society for Testing & Materials v. UpCodes, Inc., 172 F.4th 253 (3d Cir. 2026) (No. 24-2965, decided 2026-04-07)
case_law.fact: Affirmed denial of a preliminary injunction: UpCodes was likely to succeed on fair use for posting, free and verbatim, ASTM standards incorporated by reference into law (via the 2018 IBC as adopted). Preliminary-injunction stage, not a final judgment.
case_law.read: U.S. Copyright Office summary and opinion text

case_law.cite: American Society for Testing & Materials v. Public.Resource.Org, Inc., 82 F.4th 1262 (D.C. Cir. 2023); earlier 896 F.3d 437 (D.C. Cir. 2018)
case_law.fact: Non-commercial posting of standards incorporated by reference into law held fair use (2023). Followed by the Third Circuit in 2026 per a secondary report.
case_law.status: citation from general knowledge; opinion not opened in this pass

case_law.cite: Veeck v. Southern Building Code Congress International, 293 F.3d 791 (5th Cir. 2002) (en banc)
case_law.fact: Model building codes, once enacted as law, could be copied as 'the law' of the enacting jurisdictions.
case_law.status: citation from general knowledge; not opened in this pass

case_law.fact: Government edicts doctrine: works authored by judges and legislators in the course of official duties are not copyrightable. Concerned annotations authored by a legislative body, not privately authored model codes.
case_law.status: citation from general knowledge; not opened in this pass

case_law.cite: Building Officials & Code Administrators v. Code Technology, Inc., 628 F.2d 730 (1st Cir. 1980)
case_law.fact: Early case doubting enforceable copyright in a model code adopted as state law.
case_law.status: citation from general knowledge; not opened in this pass

case_law.cite: County of Santa Clara v. Superior Court (2009) 170 Cal.App.4th 1301
case_law.fact: California public agencies may claim copyright in public records only where a statute expressly allows it (Public Records Act context).

notes: Main finding: of the checks listed, California changed one number: guard height is 42 in (IRC 2024: 36 in), CRC R321.1.2. All other listed building values equal IRC 2024, though several clauses carry added California exceptions or references.
The 2025 CRC keeps IRC 2024 chapter 3 numbering. Aging-in-place is R328 (not R327); sprinklers are R309 (not R313); WUI materials left the CRC for Part 7 (R337 is a pointer only).

Receptacle and lighting-outlet rules come from the California Electrical Code (NEC 2023), with no California amendment to 210.52 or 210.70; the IRC E39xx clause numbers in the us-irc-2024 pack do not apply in California. CRC R328.1.2 adds outlet and switch heights (15 to 48 in).

read_in_source is true only where the value or status was seen on an official code page (errata buff pages, emergency supplement blue pages) or, for edition facts, on an official BSC/HCD document. up.codes readings, HCD summary forms and rulemaking express terms are marked false.

California amendments were identified on up.codes by its italic styling of California text, then cross-checked for chapter 3 against the official Matrix Adoption Table. Chapters 4 and 5 were not cross-checked against a matrix.
Footing tables R403.1(1)-(3), framing span tables and energy values were not compared with IRC 2024 in this pass. California energy values come from Part 6, not IRC chapter 11.
SI figures under mm_printed / m2_printed are the code's own printed conversions; other SI figures are computed here.

Local amendments: cities and counties may amend Title 24 for local climatic, geological or topographical conditions with findings filed with BSC; AB 130 restricts new residential amendments from 2025-10-01 to 2031-06-01.

Errata and the checked clauses: the January 2026 CRC errata replaced chapter 3 pages 3-1 to 3-4 (matrix), 3-23/24 (R302), 3-35 to 3-38 and 3-41 to 3-46 (R305 to R309 sprinkler text) and 3-83/84 (R336 to R340). None of the checked clauses R310 to R328 is on a replaced page, so the errata did not change them.
